title: Cylinder 9 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Performance
plain: The cylinder 9 deactivation/intake valve control is not responding the way the computer expects. Cylinder deactivation shuts off some cylinders while cruising to save fuel, and this circuit controls cylinder 9.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel-saving cylinder shutoff may be disabled
Possible misfire, rough running or ticking noise

causes.name: Low or dirty engine oil, or the wrong oil thickness
Sticking cylinder 9 deactivation solenoid or clogged oil screen

checks: Check the engine oil level and condition first
Check for misfire codes on the same cylinder
Command the solenoid with a scan tool and listen or watch for a response
fix: Correct the oil level and type first; if the code returns, replace the solenoid, and in some cases the lifter.

title: Cylinder 9 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the cylinder 9 deactivation/intake valve control circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. Cylinder deactivation shuts off some cylinders while cruising to save fuel, and this circuit controls cylinder 9.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel-saving cylinder shutoff may be disabled
Possible misfire, rough running or ticking noise

causes.name: Control wire to the cylinder 9 deactivation solenoid shorted to ground

checks: Inspect the wiring in the cylinder 9 deactivation/intake valve control circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Check the wiring for a short to ground with a meter
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the cylinder 9 deactivation solenoid.

title: Cylinder 9 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the cylinder 9 deactivation/intake valve control circuit and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. Cylinder deactivation shuts off some cylinders while cruising to save fuel, and this circuit controls cylinder 9.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel-saving cylinder shutoff may be disabled
Possible misfire, rough running or ticking noise

causes.name: Control wire to the cylinder 9 deactivation solenoid shorted to voltage or the part open inside

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the cylinder 9 deactivation/intake valve control circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the open ground or shorted wire; if the wiring is fine, replace the cylinder 9 deactivation solenoid.

title: Cylinder 9 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer is watching the cylinder 9 exhaust valve control circuit and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. Cylinder deactivation shuts off some cylinders while cruising to save fuel, and this circuit controls cylinder 9.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel-saving cylinder shutoff may be disabled
Possible misfire, rough running or ticking noise

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the cylinder 9 exhaust valve control solenoid
Broken or chafed wire in the cylinder 9 exhaust valve control circuit
Failed cylinder 9 exhaust valve control solenoid
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the cylinder 9 exhaust valve control circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the cylinder 9 exhaust valve control solenoid.

title: Cylinder Deactivation System Bank 2
plain: The system that shuts off some cylinders to save fuel while cruising is not working correctly on bank 2 of the engine. The computer usually turns the feature off until it is fixed.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Lower fuel economy
Rough running or misfire in some cases
ECO or fuel-saving indicator may stop coming on

causes.name: Engine oil low, dirty or the wrong thickness
Faulty cylinder deactivation oil pressure switch or sensor
Sticking cylinder deactivation solenoid or clogged screen
Wiring or connector fault at the solenoids
Stuck deactivating lifters or rocker arms

checks: Check the oil level and make sure the correct oil is used
Look for other cylinder deactivation or misfire codes
Check the oil pressure switch and solenoid operation with a scan tool
fix: Often fixed with an oil change to the correct oil; otherwise replace the oil pressure switch or deactivation solenoid.

cost.job: Replace cylinder deactivation solenoid or oil pressure switch

examples: Seen on Honda V6 engines with Variable Cylinder Management, such as the Odyssey and Pilot
drive: Usually drivable while you get it checked soon. Check the oil level, since low oil is a common cause. If the engine misfires, runs rough, the check engine light flashes or the oil pressure light comes on, stop driving and get it checked.
test_first: Check oil level, condition and pressure, then test the bank 2 cylinder deactivation solenoids and wiring and check for lifter faults before replacing parts.
